gap: No result ChatGPT got states the price per liter of build volume at today's maker-store prices. On that measure the QIDI Max4 is the cheapest of ChatGPT's five picks at $20.29/L, the Prusa CORE One L+ costs about three times as much at $62.32/L, and the Anycubic Kobra S1 Max, which ChatGPT left out, comes in lower than all of them at $16.30/L.
standout_why: I opened desktop3dprinters.us 'Large enclosed 3D printers' (cited), desktop3dprinters.us 'Chamber temperature specs' (cited), firstlayerlab.com 'Large 3D Printers', findmy3dprinter.com 'Large Format' and scrc.us.com 'Build volume from 30 L + enclosed'. The large-enclosed list and firstlayerlab print liters and prices side by side, but neither divides one by the other. When asked to quote only page text, the chamber-specs page showed launch prices and mm volumes with no liters and no $/L. findmy3dprinter and scrc show no prices at all. Every page that has prices uses launch or October prices: $1,149 for the Max4, $1,299 or $1,199 for the K2 Plus and $749 for the Plus5. Today the maker stores charge less: $1,049, $899 and $699.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's 'best for maximum size' pick. Among its five, the QIDI Max4 is both the largest (51.7 L) and the cheapest per liter ($20.29). Against the K2 Plus, it gives 8.84 L more for $150 more, about $17 per extra liter. It also shows the Prusa CORE One L+ costs about three times as much per liter, so it only makes sense for serviceability. And it brings in the Anycubic Kobra S1 Max, which ChatGPT left out: it has the same 42.9 L as the K2 Plus for $200 less. The H2S could not be ranked because its US store price page would not open.

Chamber heater wattage for each candidate, which I wanted for a W-per-liter heating figure: none of the maker pages I opened state it. Prusa gives only whole-printer 'Preheating: ~630W'. findmy3dprinter says the K2 Plus has 'an 800W heated chamber', but I could not confirm that on a Creality page.
